### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via IApprovalService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via IApprovalService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bac9d60dc1368016061b7b59f2733c0c169f1001` — the merge of head `f4d534bd32cb18f6a350e67a7eb88469d78b53d2` into base `55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bac9d60dc1368016061b7b59f2733c0c169f1001 && git checkout bac9d60dc1368016061b7b59f2733c0c169f1001
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c f4d534bd32cb18f6a350e67a7eb88469d78b53d2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c && git merge --no-ff f4d534bd32cb18f6a350e67a7eb88469d78b53d2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `74870830a7908f70235f91a0a11b07fef65dd41b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`recall` 5577-5625, `sendBack` 6032-6140, `resubmit` 6186-6260, `assertReviseEdge` 6278-6312, `actsAsSubmitter` 1114-1117, `isOverrideActor` 2111-2165, `resolveActor` 2254-2262, `serviceResume`), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts (`runTriggerUser` 107-112, `submitterId` 199), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-revise-node.ts 70-110, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts 6298-6423, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/later-step-original-submitter.integration.test.ts 322-330, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts 663-778, packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts 440-523, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts 2448-2491, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts 190-197 and 320-345, packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts 209-230 and 500-530, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts 5950-6060, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts 1738-1744 (`cancelRun`). Remainder of the diff (`content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`, `.changeset/29910-no-submitter-returned-docs.md`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the guide paragraph was read only to check it says the same as the docblocks.

### ① Derived judgments

Read from the tree at `74870830`, not from the PR body.

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The only hunks in `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` are inside three JSDoc blocks (`recall` +6 lines, `sendBack` +5 lines, `resubmit` 1 sentence rewritten). No key, type, enum, parameter or return shape moves; `IApprovalService.recall / sendBack / resubmit` signatures are byte-identical to `origin/main`. Nothing a consumer compiles against changes.
- **Public surface: prose only, but published — right that it is treated as published.** The spec package builds `.d.ts` through tsup's dts pass (`packages/spec/tsup.config.ts:476`, `dts: { only: true, ... }`), which carries JSDoc; the amended sentences therefore ship in `@objectstack/spec`'s declaration files. That is why a changeset is owed (see ②), not `skip-changeset`.
- **`recall` docblock claim "A request with no submitter ... has no one on the `returned` arm" — right.** `actsAsSubmitter` (approval-service.ts:1114-1117) answers `false` for every actor when `submitter_id` is null; `overrideAdmits` (5613-5614) is ANDed with `raw.status === 'pending'`, so on `returned` neither the system context nor the override actor passes. Pinned at approval-service.test.ts:6403-6416 (tenant admin refused recall of a returned no-submitter request) and 6361-6395 (reader/approver refused).
- **Claim "Its way out of `returned` is a system-context `resubmit`" — right, with one completeness gap (④ S2/S4).** `resubmit` (6202) admits `context.isSystem` regardless of submitter; pinned at approval-service.test.ts:6418-6423. `isSystem` is never resolved from inbound HTTP (rest-server.ts:2448, 2488) and the REST `/resubmit` route passes the caller's own context (approvals-routes.ts:518-523), so the call is server-side only, as the docblocks imply and the guide states.
- **Claim "opens the next round `pending`, again with no submitter" — right.** The send-back resume (6140-6146) and the resubmit resume (6241-6248) carry no `resumedBy`; `serviceResume` adds only the `RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE` marker; `deciderSegmentContext` (run-resume.ts:326-327) switches identity only on a `resumedBy`. The run context therefore stays the trigger's, and the re-entered approval node stamps `submitterId: runTriggerUser(context)` (approval-node.ts:199), which is `null` for a context with no `userId` / a recorded `triggerUserId: null` (107-112). The exact round-N+1 case is not pinned by a test (the integration pin at later-step-original-submitter.integration.test.ts:322 covers a later step, not a resubmitted round); the code path is unambiguous.
- **Claim "where the `pending` arm's system context or override actor may recall it" — right.** 5613-5618 with `isOverrideActor` (2111-2113: `context.isSystem` passes; platform/tenant admin by posture or grant; a null-org request may be released by any tenant admin). Pinned at approval-service.test.ts:6403-6416 and 6418-6421.
- **`sendBack` docblock claim "A request with no submitter is sent back the same way" — right.** `sendBack` (6032-6050) tests the actor against the pending slate or `isSystem`, never the submitter; `assertReviseEdge` (6278-6312) requires a `revise` edge into an `approval_revise` node. Pinned by the test battery's `sendBack` helper on no-submitter requests (6341-6346).
- **`resubmit` docblock rewrite "by the submitter or a system context (the system context alone on a request with no submitter)" — right**, and it now agrees with `ApprovalResubmitInput.actorId`'s existing text (L825) and with the code comment at 6201.
- **Guide paragraph vs docblocks — consistent.** The guide's trigger list (schedule, time-relative, api, record-change fired by a system write) matches the engine's own statement (runtime-identity.ts:508-514; run-resume.ts:191-197). One guide-only nit for the lane seat, outside ④: the guide says "`IApprovalService.resubmit` with `isSystem: true`" but `resolveActor` (2254-2258) throws `VALIDATION_FAILED: actorId is required` for a system context that names no actor, so the call also needs `actorId` (the battery passes `SYSTEM_ACTOR`).
- **Nothing else in the diff implies a judgment.** No generated artifact moves (`api-surface/contracts.json` records interface names only; the dev reports `check:generated` clean; `Spec property liveness` and `Check Changeset` are green on the head).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29910-no-submitter-returned-docs.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch` — **matches what the diff publishes.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3: `skip-changeset` is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package; this diff ships amended JSDoc in `@objectstack/spec`'s `.d.ts` output, so `patch` is the floor and the ceiling (no kind, no key, no behaviour).
- `Clause-②: no` on both the PR body and the changeset body — right: no capability is widened or narrowed at any consumer; the three verbs admit exactly whom they admitted on `main`. No `(widening)` / `(narrowing)` arm, so no narrowing face and no BREAKING banner is owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` on both — right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag (os-dev-report, `out_of_scope_findings`, repeated in the PR's Acceptance notes):** "the documented way out works in code but has no door a user can reach (a system-context resubmit needs server-side code). Is a guide line that relies on server-side code enough to satisfy option D?"
  **Answer against the ruling text: yes, and it is the only thing D permits.** The card quotes D verbatim as "leave the behaviour as it is and document the way out (chosen)", and its own "What" section names that way out as "a system-context `resubmit` opens a fresh `pending` round". The card closes with "⛔ No behaviour change." A system context is server-side by construction (rest-server.ts:2448: "`isSystem` flags are never set on inbound HTTP"), so the way out the maintainer accepted is a server-side one; opening a console or REST door for it would be a behaviour change the ruling forbids and would re-open the A/B debate the ruling closed. The documentation therefore satisfies D exactly when it says plainly that the exit is server-side code in a system context — which the guide does in those words and the `sendBack` docblock does ("only when server-side code will make that call"). Not escalated. If the maintainer later wants a user-reachable door, that is a new card with its own ruling, not a defect of this PR.
- **Dev deviations:** spec vitest not run locally (left to CI `Test Core`, in progress at review time — see below); `git fetch --unshallow` in the shared store. Neither touches the tree under review.
- **No `open_questions` entry on the card beyond the flag above.** The triage comment (6602125866) carries no question. The claim comment's `Premise: holds` was re-checked: on `origin/main` the `recall` input docblock (L665-668) and the `recall` method docblock (L1035-1040) still say `returned` is the submitter's alone, and no guide paragraph on `main` states the no-submitter path.
- **Check-runs on `74870830` at review time:** success — Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint & Repo Gates and every `Lint ·` family, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label, filter. Still in progress — Test Core (1-8/8), Test UI (1-16/16), Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check UI. Skipped (opt-in or not applicable) — Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness, Lint UI, Schedule gate. No check-run has failed. The in-progress families cannot be contradicted by a comments-only spec diff (non-comment token stream unchanged, verified by reading the hunks), but their conclusions are the gate verdicts and the seat should see them green before landing.

### ④ Design judgment

`hits` file: `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`. Judged against the code it cites on `origin/main` and against ruling D as quoted on the card.

**Attempts to break it, each answered by the tree:**
1. *Is anyone admitted on the `returned` arm after all?* No — `actsAsSubmitter` fails closed for every actor; `overrideAdmits` is pending-only; `inReviseWindow` only widens the state check. Test battery 6361-6416 pins every reader class.
2. *Could the REST `/resubmit` route be the door the docblock says does not exist?* No — it forwards `context` as resolved by `resolveExecCtx`, which never sets `isSystem` (rest-server.ts:2448, 2488); the console `approval_resubmit` action is gated on `viewer.is_submitter` (sys-approval-request.object.ts:775), and `attachViewers` cannot answer true for a null submitter.
3. *Could the system-context resubmit itself be refused?* It passes 6202; it still owes `assertLatestForRun`, the colliding-pending check and `assertRunResumable`, which are the same guards every resubmit owes and the docblock's pre-existing text already covers ("LATEST `returned` request of its (run, node)"). `resolveActor` needs an `actorId` for a system caller — the contract's `ApprovalResubmitInput.actorId` is already a required `string`, so the docblock is not wrong, only the guide's shorthand is loose (noted in ①).
4. *Does round N+1 really open with no submitter, or does the system caller become the submitter?* No switch happens (no `resumedBy` on either resume; `runTriggerUser` never falls through to the decider: approval-node.ts:103-105 "⛔ Not `triggerUserId ?? userId`"). The claim holds for `runAs:'user'` and `runAs:'system'` flows alike.
5. *Is a system-context resubmit the ONLY exit?* For the request row and the flow's forward path, yes. An operator `IAutomationService.cancelRun` (automation-service.ts:1744, optional) also ends the parked run, but it discards the branch and leaves the row `returned`; it has no REST route either (none in `packages/rest/src`). So the docblock's sentence is true but not complete — see S2.

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix:**
- **S1 — the same published file now contradicts itself on `resubmit`.** The `reissueContinuation` docblock (head L1145-1147) still says "{@link resubmit} is still no way back — it is submitter-only", while the amended `resubmit` docblock (L1070-1072) says "by the submitter or a system context". One phrase ("submitter-or-system, and it owes the `resubmit` edge ...") restores consistency; the second half of that sentence (the edge argument) is still the load-bearing reason and stays.
- **S2 — the `sendBack` author rule is under-scoped for the common user-less case.** "a flow whose trigger resolves no user declares the `revise` edge only when server-side code will make that call" is followable for `schedule` / `time_relative` / `api` triggers (always user-less) but not for a `record_change` flow, which the engine names the most common user-less run (runtime-identity.ts:508-514: fired by a system write it carries no user; fired by a user's write it carries one). An author of such a flow cannot drop the `revise` edge without taking send-back away from every user-submitted round. The docblock should say: for a trigger that never resolves a user, declare `revise` only when server-side code will resubmit; for a record-change flow, a round opened by a system write that is sent back parks until server-side code resubmits it (or an operator `cancelRun` discards the run, leaving the row `returned`). The guide's parallel sentence inherits the same gap; lane seat's call there.
- **S3 — pre-existing, two lines above the inserted paragraph, not this PR's hunk.** The `recall` docblock's `returned` arm (L1037-1038) says "the run resumes down `reject` the same way", but a recall in the revise window calls `cancelRun` (approval-service.ts:5683-5694) and the guide says "A recall from the revise window cancels the run" (approvals.mdx:770-771). Since the PR edits this very docblock, folding the one-line correction in is cheap; otherwise it is a separate docs card. Not counted against this PR.

**Verdict on the design:** the three docblock additions are true at every cited point in the live tree, say nothing the ruling did not accept, and change no accept set. The gaps found are completeness and consistency of published prose, none of which misleads a consumer into a call the code refuses or omits a refusal the code makes — should-fix, not must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-29910-no-submitter-returned-docs`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f4d534bd32cb18f6a350e67a7eb88469d78b53d2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`recall` revise-window arm 5680-5705, `resolveActor` 2254-2258, `resubmit` 6202), packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts (`cancelRun` 883-925, user-less warning 190-197), packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts 500-530, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts 2035-2047 (record-change hook session), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts 1195-1260 (`isRunLifecycleWrite`, platform-operator gate), packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts 2006-2008 and 961 (cancel route under `/api/v1`), packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts 1738-1744 (`cancelRun`). Remainder of the delta (`content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; read to check it says the same as the docblocks.

This is a DELTA record over the PASS rendered on `74870830a7908f70235f91a0a11b07fef65dd41b`. Judged: `git diff 74870830 f4d534bd` (2 files, +21 / -11; one commit, parent `74870830`, no merge of `main`). Everything that record found true at `74870830` is untouched by the delta and is not re-argued here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: still unchanged — right.** The delta's hunks in `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` are all inside JSDoc (`*`-prefixed lines only; a filter of the diff for non-comment added or removed lines is empty). No signature, key, type or enum moves. The `.changeset` is unchanged and still `'@objectstack/spec': patch`.
- **Published-prose claims introduced by the delta, each checked against the live tree:**
  - `recall` docblock, `returned` arm: "the run is cancelled (the revise window has no `reject` edge to resume down)" — **right.** approval-service.ts:5680-5694: `if (inReviseWindow) { // the run is paused at the revise-window node, which has no reject out-edge to resume down — terminally cancel it instead ... this.automation!.cancelRun!(runId, ...) }`. Replaces the pre-existing wrong sentence (my S3). Now agrees with the guide (approvals.mdx:770-771).
  - `sendBack` docblock: "a flow whose trigger never carries a user (schedule, time-relative, api) declares the `revise` edge only when server-side code will make that call" — **right.** runtime-identity.ts:510-511 names `time_relative` and `api` as supplying no user, and 282/354 the schedule; the engine's build-time lint `flow-runas-unscoped` treats these as the statically decidable user-less shapes (engine.ts:5965-5967).
  - `sendBack` docblock: "A record-change flow has no submitter only when a system write fired it" — **right, in the engine's own words.** run-resume.ts:196-197: "a record-change flow fired by a system write carries no user either (ADR-0049)"; runtime-identity.ts:508-510: user-less "most often a record-change flow fired by a write that carried no user". The record-change hook session carries the writer's `userId` (plugin.ts:2037), so a user's write always yields a submitter and only a no-user (system) write yields none.
  - `sendBack` docblock: "that round, sent back, waits for the call, or an operator's `cancelRun` discards the run and leaves the request `returned`" — **right.** `cancelRun` (run-resume.ts:883-925) only `forgetSuspendedRun(run, 'cancelled')` and records a `cancelled` history row; it never touches `sys_approval_request`, and plugin-approvals registers no run-cancelled listener (grep for `run.cancelled` / `onRunCancelled` / `runCancelled` in plugin-approvals and service-automation: none). So the row stays `returned` and the record stays unlocked (send-back already unlocked it).
  - `reissueContinuation` docblock: "{@link resubmit} is still no way back — it is by the submitter or a system context only, and it owes the `resubmit` edge where the stranded continuation was the `revise` one" — **right**, and it now matches the amended `resubmit` docblock (my S1). The load-bearing half (the edge argument) is kept verbatim.
- **Guide paragraph vs docblocks — consistent, and the two new guide-only claims hold:** (i) "`IApprovalService.resubmit` with `isSystem: true`, and an `actorId` naming the acting identity, which a system caller must supply" — `resolveActor` (approval-service.ts:2254-2258) throws `VALIDATION_FAILED: actorId is required` for a system context with no actor (the actorId nit, resolved). (ii) "a platform operator's `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/runs/:runId/cancel` discards the run and leaves the request `returned`" — the route is mounted at `${base}/automation/:name/runs/:runId/cancel` with `base` defaulting to `/api/v1` (dispatcher-plugin.ts:2006, 961) and gated by `isRunLifecycleWrite` to platform-operator standing (domains/automation.ts:1195-1260: "a platform-operator verb ... a run belongs to the environment rather than to a user"). This is the one user-reachable exit for the parked run, and the guide names it correctly as the operator's door, not as a way to move the request on.
- **No new generated artifact or surface implied.** `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green on `f4d534bd`.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged from `74870830`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset body — still right. The delta adds and corrects published JSDoc only; no key, type, behaviour or accept set moves; the docblock text ships in the `.d.ts` output (tsup dts pass), so `patch` is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3).
- `Check Changeset` on `f4d534bd`: success.
- Nit, not a finding: the changeset body lists the `recall` / `sendBack` / `resubmit` docblocks; the delta also corrects one sentence in the `recall` `returned` arm (covered by "recall") and one phrase in the `reissueContinuation` docblock (not named). Harmless for a `patch` of comment text; the seat may add four words if it wants the changelog exact.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The four items from my record on `74870830`, each resolved without a new wrong claim:**
  - S1 (`reissueContinuation` said `resubmit` is "submitter-only") — resolved; new wording verified above.
  - S2 (`sendBack` author rule under-scoped for record-change flows) — resolved; the rule is now scoped to schedule / time-relative / api, and the record-change case is stated with both real outcomes (server-side resubmit, or operator `cancelRun` discarding the run and leaving the row `returned`). The guide carries the parallel sentence and names the concrete operator door.
  - S3 (pre-existing "the run resumes down `reject`" in the `recall` `returned` arm) — resolved in this PR; verified against approval-service.ts:5680-5694.
  - actorId nit (guide's `isSystem: true` shorthand) — resolved in the guide; the spec's `ApprovalResubmitInput.actorId` was already a required `string`, so no docblock change was owed there.
- **The dev's original open question** (is a server-side-only way out enough for ruling D?) was answered yes on `74870830` against the ruling text; the delta does not reopen it. The guide now additionally names the one user-reachable operator door (`cancelRun`), which discards rather than moves the run, so the answer stands: documenting the system-context resubmit as the way the request moves on is exactly what D ("leave the behaviour as it is and document the way out", "⛔ No behaviour change") permits. Not escalated.
